newsitem.title: CHINA: Ssangyong chief says China costs high.
newsitem.headline: Ssangyong chief says China costs high.

text.p: The cost of doing business in China is high and arbitrary regulations could have a negative effect on the nation's economy, Kim Suk Joon, chairman of South Korea's Ssangyong Business Group said on Tuesday.

While China had much economic potential, Beijing should not ignore the experience of neighbouring countries that had priced themselves out of the market for foreign investment, he told a business gathering in Beijing.
Total business costs in China "may be higher than in competing countries", Kim said.

He said investors faced new costs from the abolition of tax breaks for imports of capital equipment, the lowering of rebates for exports and the introduction of a 10 percent guarantee fee on imports of raw materials.
"I believe these difficulties are to be expected in a transitional period," he said.
But he added that South Korea, once highly attractive to foreign investors, saw investment diverted away in the 1990s because of a less favourable business environment.
He attributed this to high wages, high interest rate levels and excessive government regulation.
Earlier on Tuesday, China's official media said Ssangyong Group's Ssangyong Corp had reached an agreement for a telecommunications project in Beijing worth up to $200 million.
